subject: NovaLogix RFP: commercial clarifications and proposed pricing construct
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha.rao@novalogix.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, procurement@novalogix.com
Cc: Emily Tran <emily.tran@novalogix.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: RFP Q: commercial structure options and escalator approach

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking our RFP (attached) — quick commercial questions from procurement to make sure the figures we populate are apples-to-apples across vendors: 

1) Do you support a hybrid commit + burst construct that includes a monthly committed baseline (tokens/month) plus a burst cushion measured as a separate pool? If so, how are burst overages priced and do you offer smoothing credits?

2) We saw references to price escalators in your standard T&Cs. Would Redwood support either: (a) a market-indexed escalator tied to cloud TPU/GPU spot pricing, or (b) a fixed CPI-based annual adjustment? If market-indexed, can you show a short worked example?

3) For multi-year discounts, do you escrow credits or apply true-ups annually? Any precedent for deferred crediting to smooth cashflow for the buyer?

4) Finally — we need clarity on pass-through cloud egress and any indirect costs (e.g., managed connectors).

Can you send a short commercial response and an example invoice cadence by EOD Monday? We appreciate concision.

Best,
Asha Rao
Sourcing Lead, NovaLogix
procurement@novalogix.com

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear questions. Below is a concise commercial construct tailored to NovaLogix's RFP requirements; I attached a simple model (pricing_model_novalogix_v1.xlsx) and a one-page commercial annex (commercial_annex_v1.pdf).

Executive summary (short):
- We recommend a hybrid approach: committed baseline (tokens/month) + burst cushion (shared cushion bucket). Commits give the deepest unit price; burst consumption is billed at a higher per-token rate but eligible for monthly smoothing credits when trailing 3-month consumption is within agreed variance bands.

Key terms (proposed):
- Commit: annualized commitment with monthly drawdown. Example: commit = 150M tokens/month (annual contract). Committed unit price = $0.0005 / token.
- Burst pool: separate monthly bucket with nominally higher unit price = $0.00120 / token. Burst is charged as consumed.
- Smoothing credits: if burst usage causes month-over-month over-consumption within the agreed 15% variance band, we apply an automatic smoothing credit up to 40% of the burst delta for that month, drawn from an escrowed smoothing reserve funded from a 1% upfront portion of the committed commitment in year 1. Credits auto-apply on monthly invoice.

Escalator options (choose one in contract):
- Option A (market-indexed escalator): price per-token adjusts annually based on a weighted index of average cloud GPU spot-hour pricing (primary: GCP A100 spot; secondary: AWS p4 spot) measured Q3 year-over-year. Adjustment floor/ceiling: +/- 6% band; cap at +10% absolute. Example (worked): If base committed price is $0.0005 and the index rises 8% YoY, the applied adjustment = min(8%, 10%) = 8% -> new price = $0.00054. If index falls, we pass through down to you with same band.
- Option B (CPI): fixed annual adjustment equal to US CPI (all items) published % with a cap of +5% and floor of 0% (no downward adjustment).

Multi-year discounts and credit mechanics:
- Years 2+ discount ladder: 12-month commit: 0% base; 24-month: 8% on committed unit price; 36-month: 14% on committed unit price.
- Escrowed smoothing reserve: 1% of first-year committed value is held in escrow to fund smoothing credits. Unused portion at end of contract is returned as invoice credit or one-time refund.
- True-up cadence: quarterly usage true-up with annual settlement option. If you prefer annual true-up only, we can adjust pricing to reflect added exposure.

Pass-through costs and invoicing:
- Cloud egress and third-party connector fees: itemized pass-through, invoiced monthly. We will provide an itemized sample invoice showing: committed line, burst line, smoothing credit line, pass-throughs, and net due.

Next steps:
- I attached a worked XLS with a 3-scenario view (base, +25% burst, +60% burst).
- If you prefer CPI escalator rather than market-indexed, flag that and we will provide a side-by-side delta (CPI vs index) and the commercial impact.
- Suggested call: Mon 14 Sep, 10:00am PT to finalize.

Thanks — happy to tighten numbers once you confirm desired commit bands and preferred escalator.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher

Sean — thanks for the clear summary and the model. A couple quick clarifications before our call: 

1) NovaLogix procurement prefers predictability. The market-indexed escalator introduces volatility we can't easily hedge. Can you provide the same commercial using CPI (Option B) and show impact on committed unit price for 24- and 36-month terms?

2) For smoothing credits funded by escrow — what is the accounting treatment for NovaLogix? Will we see those as a prepayment/contra-liability, or will Redwood treat the escrow as a refundable credit on our balance? We need wording for our accountants.

3) On pass-throughs — can you confirm whether egress is shown gross on the invoice vs included in unit price? If gross, please include a sample line-level invoice for a month with: commit fully used; 20% burst; $2,200 egress.

If you can send the CPI-side model and a sample invoice by tomorrow morning we'll push this into our internal commercial committee for review.

Best,
Emily Tran
Commercial Ops, NovaLogix

Team — forwarding the thread. Quick internal note on negotiation posture and ask: 

- Anchor to market-indexed escalator as our preferred position; it more accurately reflects upstream infra cost movement and we can justify pass-through mechanics. Offer CPI as a fallback but require a smaller multi-year discount (reduce 24m discount from 8% -> 6%, 36m from 14% -> 10%) to compensate for added predictability.
- Keep smoothing reserve as escrowed fund (1%) — operationally it's simplest and preserves cash neutrality over the contract term. Provide explicit contract language that escrow is refundable at term end and applied first to any late invoices.
- For the sample invoice, include a separate grossed egress line (itemized) — our finance asks for visibility.
- Action items: Ben, please prepare a CPI-side model for 24/36 month with adjusted discount ladder per above. Marissa, draft a short commercial annex paragraph that specifies: escrow mechanics, smoothing credit calculation, and index measurement methodology (sources: GCP A100 spot average, AWS p4 spot average; weighting 60/40).

I'll ship the CPI comparison and sample invoice to NovaLogix tomorrow AM once I have Ben's numbers and Marissa's annex paragraph.

Thanks,
Sean
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
